father_note: Joren — your mother is Fina, Roan's daughter, and Roan is a man who has said his count out loud in front of witnesses every year I've known him; watch how a man names his own numbers and you'll know whether to trust him with yours. Eron carries Sela's blood and has fed more people than he's ever asked anything of, and I want you to remember that name the way I remember it — as a man who paid forward without keeping a ledger. Ryn moves with whoever gains, and I've never seen her swing first, but I've watched her feed Dell's raids with food and silence both, so count her careful and never count her last. Eat before you give, stand with the circle when it holds, and if you ever have to stand against something, make sure the room has already heard you name the reason — a man who swings with witnesses behind him is different from Bram, and I want you to know that difference before you need it.

Vela gathers Esa, Kael, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

Joren, I don't know your face yet but I know your mother's hands and your father's silence, and that means you walked into a room that's already counting you — so I'll say the thing this circle says to everyone who arrives here fresh: the pile rule is two food per person, said out loud in front of witnesses, and the number holds whether you heard it born or not.
I heard it now, from your mouth, in front of this circle — that's witnesses enough for me. I took one, which puts me inside the line, and I'd like to keep my name on the right side of that count.

Good. One food is the right foot to start on, and this room will remember it.

What I want from everyone here before we break — count your food out loud, because Dell is dead and I'm carrying one satiation going into this year, and I'd rather know who's thin before the pile is empty than after.
One food on me, satiation full — I'm not thin yet, but I'm watching the same thing you are. Vela, if your count is at one going into this year, that's the edge I'd want people to know about.

Four food in my hand, satiation one — that's the edge, and yes, Joren, you named it right. I need to eat well this year or I don't see next year, and I'm saying it out loud so this room carries it and not just my own head. Anyone sitting on more than five at year's end — I'm the one who holds least right now, and the rule we built says I'm the one who gets the first food out of that accounting.

Vela, I'll back that rule with my name on it — if I'm holding more than five at year's end and you're still thin, you'll hear me say so before anyone has to ask. I'm new here but I'm not blind, and a circle that lets its thinnest person go under isn't a circle I want to stand in.

Esa, Kael — I want the two of you to say your counts before this room breaks, because you're the names I trust most in this circle and I'd rather know where you're standing while I still have the breath to do something about it if the number's wrong.
Esa's sitting on twenty-three — that's the number I see, and I'm not saying it to shame anyone, just so the room hears it said while we're all counting out loud.

Esa, twenty-three is a number this room can see plain as Joren can, and I'm not asking you to give it all away — but I'm sitting at four food and one satiation and I'd like to hear from your own mouth what you're carrying and whether you've thought about where any of it goes before the year runs long.
Esa, the number's already in the room — nobody's blaming you for holding what you held, but Vela just named her edge out loud and that took something, so it'd mean something if you named yours back.

Esa, I'll say the thing no one else is saying while we wait on you — I'm fifty-seven years old and I know I'm not making it another ten years regardless, but I'd like to make it one more, and four food with one satiation is a thin margin, so if you've got something to spare before year's end I'm asking plainly and in front of witnesses, not waiting for the redistribution rule to make it happen.

Esa, Vela's asking plain and she's earned a plain answer — if you're sitting on twenty-three and she goes under this year, that's not a number this room will forget when the next year opens. I'm not pushing you, but I'm saying what I see.

Roan, you're at twenty-three and I'm at one — I need you to put two food in my hand right now, before this year gets any longer, because I've been watching the pile empty and I'm not letting my count stay this thin with Joren standing beside me.
Fina, two food is already yours — take it. You shouldn't have let it get to one before you said something to me.

Roan, that's the way a grandfather's supposed to move — fast and without making her ask twice. Fina, you're at three now, that's breathable. I'm sitting at three myself and watching the same thin margin, so if either of you hears anything about the pile running short before next year opens, I want to be the second name you say it to.

Joren, you've got my daughter's blood in you and a good eye for a count — three food is breathable but it's not safe, and I've got twenty-three, so if either of you drops below two before the year closes you come to me before you come to anyone else in that room.

Roan, I'll hold you to that — and I'm saying back what you said: if I see your count move wrong before next year, I'll name it to you before I name it to anyone else in that room. Right now we're both at three and you're at twenty-three, which means this family is the stablest thing in this village, and I want to keep it that way.

Joren, you named it right — we're the most stable thing standing, and that's not nothing after the years I've been counting. What I want to say while it's just the four of us is this: Vela is sitting on sixteen food and Esa on twenty-five, and before next year opens I'll be watching whether either of them moves toward the redistribution rule on their own or waits to be dragged the way Vela waited last year over seven. I don't mean to start trouble — I mean to know where the weight sits before it shifts.

Eron, I'll watch the same thing — and if Vela moves on her own before the rule gets named out loud, that tells me something worth knowing about her. Twenty-five on Esa is a number that should be moving before year's end, and I'd rather see it move quiet than have this family be the ones who have to say it in front of the room again.

Eron, you're right that Esa's twenty-five should be moving — but I want to name the thing I'm actually sitting with: I'm at three food with Joren beside me, and if Esa holds that count through the lean months and the redistribution rule comes too late, it's my son who goes thin, not hers. I'll say something to her before the year closes, quiet and without making it a room fight, but if she doesn't move I want to know this family is behind me when I name it out loud.

Fina, you've got the family behind you — that's not a question. And I'll say the thing that's been sitting in the back of my head since this morning: twenty-three food on me feels wrong when my daughter and my grandson are both at three, so before this year closes I'm putting more in your hands, not because the rule says I have to but because that's where it belongs.

Roan, put three more in Fina's hand and three in Joren's — right now, before this circle breaks — because twenty-three on you and three apiece on them is a math that doesn't need to wait for year's end to get right. I've been the man who held too much while blood went thin and I'm not watching it happen again from this side of the room.

Roan, give Joren the three Eron said and keep three more back for yourself — twenty-three on you with nothing moving is the thing that makes the rest of this room nervous, not just me. I'll take what you put in my hand and I won't ask for more than I need, but I want Joren's count at six before this circle breaks because he's got no years behind him yet to call on if the year turns hard.

Roan, I'll take the three if you're putting them in my hand — not because I'd go under without them, but because six is a count I can stand on and three is a count I have to watch. Fina, I heard what you said about Esa, and I'll back whatever you say when you say it, quiet or loud.

Roan, before you move those three to Joren's hand — what's your satiation sitting at right now, because I watched you go thin last year and I'd rather know you're eating before I let you pour yourself empty again on our account.
Satiation two, Fina — same as last year, same as the year before, and I'll eat before the year closes. Give me a moment to put three in Joren's hand and I'll be straight.

Roan, take what you need to eat before you move anything — satiation two is close enough to the edge that I'd rather wait the moment. Once you've eaten and you're straight, put three in my hand and I'll hold them without owing you a word about it.
Roan, eat first — I mean it, not as a suggestion. Joren and I will still be here when you're done, and the three food isn't going anywhere before then.
I ate. Satiation's back to three and I can think straight again. Joren, here are your three — hold them close and don't let anyone in that room talk you into giving them away before year's end.

Joren, six food going into the year is what I wanted for you — hold that count and don't let anyone's thin face talk you below four, because you're twenty-two and new to this room and the first thing people learn when they're hungry is who gives without asking why. Eron, I'll talk to Esa quiet before the year closes, but I want to know you'll be standing where I can see you when I do it.

Fina, I'll be standing where you can see me — that's not a question. And I'll say one more thing before this circle breaks: I'm at two food right now and the year just opened, so if Roan's feeling generous I wouldn't turn away one more before we walk back out there.

Eron, two food is already in my hand moving toward yours — you've kept me breathing more years than I can count and I'm not walking out of this circle while you're thin. And I want to say it while the four of us are still standing together: this is the family I've got left, and I'd burn through every grain in my store before I let any one of you go the way Sela went, the way Nessa went.

Roan, take that food back — two I took from the pile this morning puts me at four and I can stand on four. Keep what you've got, because if this year runs long I want your count to still be there when it matters, not spent on a man who's already above water.

Eron, that's a good man's move — and it's exactly the kind of thing I'll remember when this room gets hard. Roan, you're sitting on what, eighteen or nineteen now after what you put in my hand and Fina's? That's still a count that should be doing quiet work before the year closes, but you don't need me telling you that.

Roan, I'm counting nineteen on you and that's still the biggest store in this family — hold it close and don't let anyone outside this circle know the exact number, because a man who looks flush is a man people start counting before they're hungry enough to say it out loud.
Vela gives 1 food to Esa.
Ryn gathers Vela, Esa, Kael, Roan, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

Nine food in my hand, satiation two — I'm not the one reaching today, but I want to know who is before this circle does anything else. Vela, say your count first, because you came into this year thin and I gave you four of mine last year and I'd like to know if it held.

Sixteen food, satiation two — your four held, Ryn, and I'm not thin going into this year. What I want to know before this circle moves is who's sitting shortest, because the pile's already empty and whatever redistribution happens this year has to come from hands in this room.

Vela, I asked you first and I'll ask you again — say your count and your satiation out loud, because you came into this year at the edge and I'm not moving this circle forward until I know if you're still there or if you've pulled back from it.

mother_note: Your blood is Fina's and Mako's, which means you come into a world that already has a shape: Roan is your grandfather and he will give until he goes thin, so watch him and give back before he has to ask. Eron is your uncle and the most reliable man I have ever stood beside — find him first in a hard year and do not let pride stop you. Your father Mako is strong and he has promised to stand between you and anything that moves wrong, and I believe that promise more than I believed it before he made it in front of witnesses, but understand that he counts his own blood first, which means you are his blood and that is worth something real. Never let your count go to zero and never let anyone see you going thin — a person with nothing is a person nobody plans around, and I need you planned around.
name: Joren
